fixes.target: figure-1: Route map for adequate control
fixes.value: Flow chart titled 'Figure 1 Route map for adequate control'. It starts with two boxes side by side: 'What substances/products do you use at work and for what tasks?' and 'What substances are generated by the work or processes?', each noting you only need to record this if you have more than five employees and use or generate no substances. Both lead to the question 'Is there simple information or guidance available in the form of COSHH essentials control guidance sheets...?'; 'Yes' leads to 'Are you already following the guidance or are you able to implement the controls in the guidance easily and without help?', and 'Yes' there leads to 'Record what you are doing (if you have more than five employees) and review if there are any changes.' A 'No' at either question leads to 'You may need to seek competent advice to help you identify adequate control.' followed by recording what you are doing and reviewing for changes.

columns: Purpose for which the substance is prohibited
rows: 1 2-naphthylamine; benzidine; 4-aminodiphenyl; 4-nitrodiphenyl; their salts and any substance containing any of those compounds, in a total concentration equal to or greater than 0.1 per cent by mass.
Manufacture and use for all purposes including any manufacturing process in which a substance described in Column 1 of this item is formed.
2 Sand or other substance containing free silica.
Use as an abrasive for blasting articles in any blasting apparatus.

3 A substance (a) containing compounds of silicon calculated as silica to the extent of more than 3 per cent by weight of dry material, other than natural sand, zirconium silicate (zircon), calcined china clay, calcined aluminous fireclay, sillimanite, calcined or fused alumina, olivine; or (b) composed of or containing dust or other matter deposited from a fettling or blasting process.
Use as a parting material in connection with the making of metal castings.
Use in the cold-cure process of vulcanising in the proofing of cloth with rubber.

Use for oiling the spindles of self-acting mules.

7 Ground or powdered flint or quartz other than: (a) natural sand; or (b) ground or powdered flint or quartz which forms parts of a slop or paste.

Use for sprinkling the moulds of silica bricks, namely bricks or other articles composed of refractory material and containing not less than 80 per cent of silica.

sentences: In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 1, 2-naphthylamine; benzidine; 4-aminodiphenyl; 4-nitrodiphenyl; their salts and any substance containing any of those compounds, in a total concentration equal to or greater than 0.1 per cent by mass, are prohibited for manufacture and use for all purposes including any manufacturing process in which a substance described in Column 1 of this item is formed.

In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 2, sand or other substance containing free silica, is prohibited for use as an abrasive for blasting articles in any blasting apparatus.

In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 3, a substance (a) containing compounds of silicon calculated as silica to the extent of more than 3 per cent by weight of dry material, other than natural sand, zirconium silicate (zircon), calcined china clay, calcined aluminous fireclay, sillimanite, calcined or fused alumina, olivine; or (b) composed of or containing dust or other matter deposited from a fettling or blasting process, is prohibited for use as a parting material in connection with the making of metal castings.

In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 4, carbon disulphide, is prohibited for use in the cold-cure process of vulcanising in the proofing of cloth with rubber.

In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 5, oils other than white oil, or oil of entirely animal or vegetable origin or entirely of mixed animal and vegetable origin, are prohibited for use for oiling the spindles of self-acting mules.

In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 6, ground or powdered flint or quartz other than natural sand, is prohibited for use in relation to the manufacture or decoration of pottery for the following purposes: (a) the placing of ware for the biscuit fire; (b) the polishing of ware; (c) as the ingredient of a wash for saggars, trucks, bats, cranks, or other articles used in supporting ware during firing; and (d) as dusting or supporting powder in potters’ shops.

In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 7, ground or powdered flint or quartz other than (a) natural sand or (b) ground or powdered flint or quartz which forms parts of a slop or paste, is prohibited for use in relation to the manufacture or decoration of pottery for any purpose except: (a) use in a separate room or building for (i) the manufacture of powdered flint or quartz or (ii) the making of frits or glazes or the making of colours or coloured slips for the decoration of pottery; (b) use for the incorporation of the substance into the body of ware in an enclosure in which no person is employed and which is constructed and ventilated to prevent the escape of dust.

In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 8, dust or powder of a refractory material containing not less than 80 per cent of silica other than natural sand, is prohibited for use for sprinkling the moulds of silica bricks, namely bricks or other articles composed of refractory material and containing not less than 80 per cent of silica.
In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 9, white phosphorus, is prohibited for use in the manufacture of matches.

In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, item 10, hydrogen cyanide, is prohibited for use in fumigation except when: (a) released from an inert material in which hydrogen cyanide is absorbed; (b) generated from a gassing powder; or (c) applied from a cylinder through suitable piping and applicators other than for fumigation in the open air to control or kill mammal pests.

In the prohibition of certain substances hazardous to health for certain purposes, items 11–13 are entries repealed by REACH Enforcement Regulations 2008/2852 Schedule 10(2), paragraph 1 (June 1, 2009).
